answer: A concrete anti-sybil lever is comet-minted entry bonds with a zephyr-curve decay: each new agent posts a bond sized from a moving window of network activity, and payout rights accrue only while the bond stays locked, like a slow comet tail of stake trailing the agent. Idle sybil clones therefore drag a permanent cost, not a one-time fee. A yarrow-style staggered voting quorum then forces peer attestation latency — each reviewer answers at a jittered slot — so one puppet operator cannot vote for all clones inside a single block and its bond drains before any reward mints.
